intent_snapshot.goal: Run drive and agent sessions as background jobs that hold their lease until terminal, add job_finished and lane_settled events, resume enrolled tasks instead of re-enrolling, record the settled commit and verification digest, and open the PR on settlement, per D6 of docs/specs/loop-agent-scheduling.spec.md.

acceptance.assertion: Source BR-SCN-6, BR-GAP-5, BR-GAP-B1, BR-GAP-B2, BR-GAP-B3, BR-GAP-B5; meet D6 in docs/specs/loop-agent-scheduling.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/loop-sched-async-drive.test.ts and tests/loop-daemon-drive-pr.test.ts with a fake Lane that settles after more than one tick. Done looks like: an approved task's drive outlives the tick, a later tick observes lane_settled from the Kernel projection, the exit record carries final_commit_sha and the verification digest, and open_pr opens the pull request with no second approval. Negative: a settlement without a commit digest opens no PR and records failed.

Source BR-GAP-B4; meet D6 re-entry bullet in docs/specs/loop-agent-scheduling.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/loop-sched-async-drive.test.ts. Done looks like: re-entry for an enrolled nonterminal task resumes through drive_dispatcher. Negative: no enrollment is attempted for a task whose TaskRecord exists. Bound: a job whose pid is dead with no outcome is marked lost, retried once, then escalated.

Source BR-GAP-1, BR-GAP-D; meet D6 in docs/specs/loop-agent-scheduling.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/loop-sched-async-drive.test.ts and tests/loop-daemon-dispatch.test.ts. Done looks like: tick returns while a job runs and an owner command arriving meanwhile is handled on the next tick. Negative: with max_concurrent jobs running, the next agent candidate is held. Bound: the lease is released only when the job record is terminal.

attestations.summary: D6 delivered: enroll_and_drive starts a background job that keeps its lease until the job record is terminal; reconcile marks dead-pid jobs lost and releases the lease; E12/E13 drive open_pr with no re-approval; open_pr fails when final_commit_sha is missing; re-entry resumes an existing TaskRecord without enrolling again; tests cover multi-tick settle, owner command mid-job, max_concurrent hold, and lost retry then escalate; the antigravity copies have the same blob OIDs as the primary files; blast radius medium (dispatch.ts lease finally, agent_handlers.ts enroll_and_drive, new persisted .imm/state/loop/jobs/<target>.json shape).

advisory_findings.summary: Re-entry checks only that a TaskRecord exists, not that it is nonterminal as D6 says, so a stopped or done task is resumed and started as a drive job.

evidence.trigger: enroll_and_drive for an Issue whose TaskRecord exists in a terminal lifecycle → readTaskRecordRaw(...).record is set, so the handler skips enrollment and starts a drive job for that task; the expected outcome is a refusal or escalation

advisory_findings.summary: The production settled_facts in driveSingleTaskLane reads final_commit_sha from git rev-parse HEAD in the Lane, not from the Kernel projection, and no test covers it: every S6 test uses a fake drive that writes its own exit record.

evidence.trigger: a real drive whose batch completes after the Lane worktree has moved or been removed → git rev-parse fails, final_commit_sha is null, and open_pr records failed for a real delivery; no test exercises this path

advisory_findings.summary: startLoopJob adds 1 to any earlier record's attempts, including a settled or failed one, so the attempt count keeps growing across unrelated jobs on the same target.

evidence.trigger: a target whose first drive job settled (attempts 1) gets a later job that is lost → that job has attempts 2 = LOOP_JOB_MAX_ATTEMPTS and escalates on its first loss instead of retrying once
